questions.question: Give three benefits of mining to South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Any three: employment for hundreds of thousands of people; export income from selling minerals; taxes and royalties for government services; raw materials such as coal for electricity, iron ore and manganese for steel, platinum for catalytic converters, phosphate for fertiliser; growth of industries, towns and infrastructure.

questions.question: Explain how acid mine drainage forms and why it is harmful.
questions.expected_answer: Mining exposes sulfide minerals such as pyrite to air and water; they react to form sulfuric acid and dissolved iron; the acidic water dissolves toxic heavy metals from the rocks. When old mines flood and decant, this water flows into rivers and groundwater, killing aquatic life, making water unsafe for drinking and irrigation, and corroding pipes; it can continue for decades after mining stops.

questions.question: Describe two health impacts of mining on workers or nearby communities and one way each can be reduced.
questions.expected_answer: e.g. Silicosis from breathing silica dust: reduce by wetting rock while drilling, ventilation, dust masks and medical checks. Dust from mine dumps affecting nearby residents: reduce by vegetating dumps and spraying water. Injuries from rockfalls and accidents: reduce with roof support, safety training and protective equipment. Respiratory illness from coal power station air pollution: reduce with emission controls and using less electricity.
